stem: On a city map, Elm Street and Hill Road are straight and cross each other, as shown. One angle formed at the crossing measures \(65^{\circ}\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: The angles marked \(65^{\circ}\) and \(x^{\circ}\) are opposite each other where the two straight roads cross, so they are vertical angles.

explanation.A: Correct. The angles marked \(65^{\circ}\) and \(x^{\circ}\) are vertical angles, so they are equal.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 65\), the measure of an angle next to the 65° angle. The angle marked \(x^{\circ}\) is across from it, so it is a vertical angle.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(360 - 65\). The four angles around the crossing add up to 360°, but the angle marked \(x^{\circ}\) is only one of them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(2 \cdot 65\); vertical angles are equal, so nothing is doubled.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('B','O','D')-65)<0.1
ans=65
assert abs(ang('A','O','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
